title: 16-18. I LOOK FOR YOUR DELIVERANCE, LORD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Dan will provide justice for his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Dan will be a snake by the roadside, a viper along the path, that bites the horse's heels so that its rider tumbles backward. I look for your deliverance, Lord.'" — Gen 49:16-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Jacob describes Dan as a small snake on the path — not a powerful animal, but one capable of bringing down a horse and its rider. Small does not mean harmless, and it does not mean useless. God's people have often been the small thing that changes the outcome.

But the striking part of this passage is what interrupts it. In the middle of prophesying over his sons, Jacob suddenly breaks off and prays: "I look for your deliverance, Lord."

An old man, dying, thinking about the long future of his family — and it becomes too much. He can see enemies ahead, struggles, danger. And he does the only sensible thing: he turns to God.

That is a good instinct to develop. When thinking about the future starts to weigh on you — for your children, your country, your church — turn it into prayer rather than letting it become anxiety.

Jacob does not know how the story will end for his sons. He simply looks to the Lord for deliverance. And the deliverance God provided, in time, was greater than Jacob could have imagined: a Saviour from his own family line.

Do not carry the future. Look for His deliverance.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What thought about the future weighs on you most?
2. Do your worries usually become prayers or just anxiety?
3. Where do you need to say honestly, "I look for Your deliverance, Lord"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when the future feels heavy, turn my worry into prayer. I look for Your deliverance rather than trying to secure everything myself. Amen.
